title: DNA Barcoding Protocol for Plants and Lichens
author: Kanae Nishii

Make a master mix of End-prep buffer and End-prep enzyme (x µl per sample, plus c. ½ to 1 reaction extra, depending on the total number of samples). Add the appropriate µl master mix to each amplicon pool in the strips. Set thermal cycler lid to 75°C and incubate at 20°C for 15 mins, then 65°C for 15mins. Sequencing adaptor ligation and bead clean.
Computer updates and Flongle pore scan.

Pool the barcoded ligated samples (put approx. 2 µl - 3 µl of each sample into a single 1.5 ml LoBind tube). Remove 50 µl of the above pooled sample and put it in a new 1.5 ml LoBind tube. Perform AMPureXP bead cleaning (as previously), adding 1.4 vol. beads (e.g., 65 µl for 50 µl sample – it’s also possible to use this step to concentrate your samples by starting with more than 50 µl and increasing the volume of beads, but not increasing the elution volume). Ethanol washes - use 500 µl of 80% ethanol instead of 200 µl, to better cover the beads. Following the bead clean, elute in 32 µl sigma water, pipetting off 30 µl.

AmpureXP bead clean (I) Use the beads and the amplicons at room temp. AMPureXP beads may be light sensitive — take sensible precautions - keep in the fridge when not in use; keep out of direct light where possible. Prepare 80% ethanol (400 µl per sample — use a disposable plastic reservoir) (20 ml for 48 samples = 16 ml ethanol and 4 ml sigma water). Vortex AMPureXP beads well, then add at least 1.3x vol beads to samples (26 µl for a 20 µl sample). For speed and simplicity, add the maximum number of µl for each strip, rather than adjusting the bead volume for every sample. Re-vortex beads after the end of every strip. Mix beads and samples by vortexing (with quick spin down if needed); visually check that the layers of liquids have mixed through. Leave for > 8 minutes (or stop for lunch 😊 ); vortex again half way through if beads look like they’re settling out. Move strips to magnetic rack, wait > 1 minute or until beads pellet and liquid is clear; sometimes rotating the strips on the magnet or using the block magnet helps get a sharper pellet. Remove and dispose of supernatant, using multichannel with 200 µl tips. With the strips still on the magnetic rack, quickly add 200 µl 80% ethanol (use multichannel) — if you are too slow, the ethanol will drip. Leave ethanol covering pellets for > 30 seconds (do not mix). Remove as much ethanol as possible without disturbing the pellet, using a multichannel with 200 µl tips. Repeat ethanol wash (i.e., steps 7-10). Remove as much ethanol as possible (use a P10 or P20) and air dry for a few minutes (not too dry — pellet surface should be slightly wet/shiny not starting to crack). Working off the magnet, add 12 µl resuspension buffer (0.1X TE buffer) (mix with multichannel 10-15 times, light spin and leave for a few minutes to elute). Move the strips back to the magnet, pellet the beads, and transfer 11 µl cleaned PCR product to new strips for library prep. Dispose of the old strips with beads in them.

Nomalization II (optional) Check the concentration of the cleaned pooled amplicons using the spectrophotometer setting on the deNovix, using 1.5 µl sample for each reading; blank with 0.1X TE. Wipe clean with tissue between readings. Roughly normalize samples relative to each other using 0.1X TE, so that there are none that are significantly higher than all the others (do not normalize to the lowest concentration). (The ideal concentration is 11 ng/µl, but nanodrop readings are unreliable so do not attempt to get to this concentration…) 200 fmol (ca. 130 ng for 1000 bp amplicons) is the recommended input for Native Barcoding Kit 24 V14, for full reaction MinION runs. We use half, third or quarter reactions for End prep and Barcode ligation steps in this protocol. The NEB calculator can calculate relative mol from ng ( https://nebiocalculator.neb.com/#!/dsdnaamt )

Barcode Ligation This uses the NEBNext ultra II Ligation Module. The original ONT protocol uses NEB Blunt/TA Ligase Master Mix, but this protocol is modified to use NEBNext ultra II Ligation Module. We use either a half, third or quarter reaction. Perform all reactions on ice. Native barcodes - note that there may be barcodes that have already been totally used up; spin the barcode plate down if needed. Ligation enhancer is extremely sticky (and expensive); only insert tip of pipette into liquid and pipette very slowly). EDTA - tube supplied in NEB kit; defrost, mix and transfer into a strip before use. Starting material: end-prepped samples in strips A B C D E 1 Reagent Volume (half reaction), µl Volume (third reaction), µl Volume (quarter reaction), µl Master Mix, µl 2 End-prepped DNA 7.5 5 3.75 n/a 3 Native barcode 1.25 0.833 0.625 n/a 4 ultra II Ligation Master Mix 4.2 2.8 2.1 5 Ligation enhancer 0.14 0.09 0.07 6 Total volume 13.09 8.727 6.545 -- Volumes for master mix calculations for barcode ligation Make a master mix of Ligation Master Mix and Ligation Enhancer using the volumes in the table (e.g., for a quarter reaction, 2.17 µl per sample plus c. ½ to 1 reaction extra, depending on the total number of samples). Add barcodes to each sample (e.g., for a quarter reaction, 0.625 µl), first making a hole in the foil lid of each well in the row with a green pipette tip (use the multichannel), then pipetting barcodes into the corresponding sample strip using a 10 µl multichannel. Reseal holes with sticky foil, re-number rows, and note which barcodes have been used on the box. Make sure you record which barcodes you have added to which samples! Add master mix to each well (e.g., for a quarter reaction, 2.17 µl). Mix by pipetting. Incubate at 20°C for 20 minutes, heated lid OFF . Add EDTA to stop the reaction (half reaction 0.5 µl, third reaction 0.33 µl , quarter reaction 0.25 µl) using 10 µl multichannel, mix by pipetting, then spin down. At RBGE, the EDTA is in the nanopore box kit in the freezer — in a strip

NEB has reported that contaminants seeping out of plastic tubes affect the Flongle flow cell system. To avoid this, Sequencing Buffer (SB), Library Beads (LIB), and Flow Cell Flush (FCF) are provided in glass vials in the Flongle expansion kit. In a new LoBind tube, mix 117 µl FCF with 3 µl FCT—mix by pipetting. In another LoBind tube, make the final library and store on ice: Vortex the loading beads immediately before use. Prime the flow cell: peel back the seal tab to expose the sample port (stick the seal tab to the MinION lid), ensure there is no air gap at the end of the pipette tip and dispense just under 120 µl with the P200 (twist the top of the pipette rather than pushing down, to dispense very slowly into flongle port - to avoid flushing too rapidly and damaging pores). Load the sequencing mix: with P200, mix well immediately before dispensing as above (by twisting not pushing and ensuring no air is introduced). NB: if you do get some bubbles, go ahead with the run; there’s nothing to lose at this point! Replace seal sticker to original position. Place light blocker on flow cell. Close the device and set up sequencing run.

steps.title: Amplify target loci by PCR
steps.instruction: Set up 15‑20 µl PCR reactions for each locus (e.g., rbcL, trnL‑trnF, psbA‑trnH, ITS2) aiming for ~200 fmol (≈130 ng for a 1000 bp fragment) and run the PCR using the laboratory’s standard cycling conditions.

steps.title: Run gel electrophoresis and assess amplicons
steps.instruction: Load 3 µl of each PCR product together with 3.5 µl 1 kb+ ladder onto a 1 % agarose TBE gel, run, image the gel, and record the relative brightness of each band in an Excel sheet to estimate the amount of each amplicon to add to the pool. Keep strips on ice and avoid long storage in the fridge to prevent drying.

steps.title: Normalise and pool amplicons per sample
steps.instruction: For specimens with multiple loci, combine the amplicons proportionally to their estimated concentrations and fragment sizes so that the total pooled volume is approximately 20 µl. Skip this step if only a single amplicon is present for the sample.

steps.title: AMPureXP bead clean of pooled amplicons
steps.instruction: Calculate the required bead volume using the Excel sheet (minimum 1.3 × the pool volume), add the AMPureXP beads, mix, incubate, place on a magnetic rack, discard supernatant, wash as described in the clean‑up step, and elute the cleaned pool.

steps.title: Optional Nanodrop quantification
steps.instruction: Measure the concentration of the bead‑cleaned amplicon pools with a Nanodrop spectrophotometer and use the values for a rough normalisation before library preparation.

steps.title: End‑prep and barcode ligation (day of run)
steps.instruction: Keep all reagents on ice and perform reactions on ice. For ~1000 bp amplicons use Short Fragment Buffer (SFB). Vortex and spin down NEBNext Quick Ligation Reaction Buffer (5X); do NOT vortex the quick T4 DNA Ligase (very sticky and expensive). To the tube containing 15‑30 µl barcoded/pooled sample add the buffer and ligase, pipette 10‑20 times between each addition. Incubate 20 min at 20 °C in a thermal block with the heated lid off.

steps.title: Pool barcoded samples and bead clean‑up
steps.instruction: After ligation, combine all barcoded samples into a single pool. Add 80 µl (full‑reaction) or 40 µl (half‑reaction) AMPureXP beads (1.6 × reaction volume) to the pooled ligation product, mix by pipetting, and incubate 10 min at room temperature. Place on a magnetic rack, discard supernatant, add 125 µl SFB, flick gently to resuspend beads, quick‑spin, and place back on the magnet. Remove the SFB supernatant and repeat the SFB wash once more. Use a P10 or P20 pipette to remove any residual liquid. Add 15 µl (full) or 10 µl (half) Elution Buffer (EB), resuspend beads, incubate 37 °C for 10 min, magnetise, and transfer the supernatant (the library) to a new LoBind tube.

steps.title: Qubit quantification and dilution to Flongle specs
steps.instruction: Prepare Qubit HS master mix by adding 199 µl HS buffer to 1 µl HS reagent for each tube (add ~½ extra reaction to allow for pipetting error). Add 190 µl master mix plus 10 µl standard to each standard tube, and 199 µl master mix plus 1 µl library sample to each sample tube. Vortex, let sit a few minutes, spin down bubbles, then run the standards on the deNovix to generate a new standard curve and measure the samples. Save the .csv and calculate the average concentration from the two readings for each sample. The Flongle requires 3‑4 ng/µl; dilute the library with EB to ≈4 ng/µl, re‑measure with Qubit, and repeat dilution/measurement until the concentration falls within the required range. The final input library for the Flongle is 5‑10 fmol in 5 µl (≈3‑4 ng/µl). Store the library on ice or at 4 °C for same‑day use; for longer storage keep at –80 °C. (For a MinION run, make up the library to 12 µl at 10‑20 fmol, which corresponds to ≈10 ng/µl for 1000 bp amplicons.)

steps.title: Prepare MinION/Flongle device (morning of run)
steps.instruction: Check for computer updates, install and restart, then log in as a local user (do not log in to an ONT account). Set ‘active hours’ to the maximum 18 h, and disable news, OneDrive, etc. Plug the MinION into the computer, insert the Flongle adapter and flow cell (do not unplug later), and ensure the device sits flat. Perform a pore scan; record the number of available pores (≥50 required). Thaw Sequencing Buffer (SB), Library Beads (LIB), Flow Cell Flush (FCF), and Flow Cell Tether (FCT); vortex, spin down, and keep on ice. Write the number of uses on the expansion kit, and log the flow cell ID and pore count on the RBGE Flongle log sheet.

steps.title: Load library and start sequencing
steps.instruction: Prime the flow cell with SB and FCT according to the ONT protocol, then load the diluted library (5 µl) onto the Flongle. In MinKNOW click “Start Sequencing”, enter an experiment name (e.g., Flongle1_amplicon_2024_Feb_16), sample IDs (barcode ranges), flow cell ID, and kit ID. Choose to run until ‘end of life’ to maximise data, enable “Super accurate” basecalling, and turn on both basecalling and barcoding. Retrieve the data from /C/data/<experiment name>. If the run stops prematurely while pores are still active, attempt another run.

steps.title: Log run details and back up data
steps.instruction: Record on the RBGE Flongle log sheet the number of ligations performed, pore count, total data generated, run time, and any comments. Copy the raw data to the Z‑drive and to the Data Heap using the prescribed folder‑naming conventions, and also back up to the external hard drive provided.

steps.title: Data analysis with Petithebi pipeline
steps.instruction: Run the Petithebi pipeline (https://github.com/Gesners/petithebi) on the CropDiversity server to obtain consensus fasta files for each barcode. BLAST each consensus against NCBI to identify the locus. Use Sequencher (or similar) to trim primer and adaptor remnants, flip reverse‑oriented reads, and separate concatenated loci. Add the EDNA number and morphological ID to each fasta header (e.g., >EDNA24-0065638|Sphagnum_beothuk_consensus_barcode15.trimmed_2_0(5323)). After BLAST, annotate the header with match status (e.g., |_NOMATCH_ if no hit). If multiple copies of a marker are present, retain the copy with the highest read count. Upload the final fasta files to BOLD.
